item.title: International FASD Awareness Day
item.description:
Wednesday, 9 September 2026

Story Bridge will be lit Red to support International FASD Awareness Day

Foetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) is a lifelong disability caused by prenatal alcohol exposure and is the leading non-genetic developmental disability in Australia and the western world. Each year, more children are born with FASD than with Autism, Spina Bifida, Cerebral Palsy, and Down Syndrome combined. The 9th day of the 9th month was chosen as International FASD Awareness Day, symbolising the nine months of pregnancy and the importance of avoiding alcohol during this time to prevent FASD. The National Organisation for Foetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (NOFASD) has been Australia's peak body for more than 25 years, supporting individuals and families living with FASD and promoting awareness, prevention, diagnosis, and improved outcomes. Throughout September (FASD Awareness Month), we intensify our efforts to raise community awareness of FASD, including wearing red shoes, socks and clothing and lighting up public landmarks in red to spark conversations about FASD.

This Light Up is organised by: NOFASD Australia Limited

item.title: Bravehearts Day
item.description:
Friday, 11 September 2026

Story Bridge will be lit Purple to support Bravehearts Day

Bravehearts Day 2026 is on Friday 11 September, during National Child Protection Week.
Bravehearts Day is dedicated to raising funds and awareness for the prevention of child sexual abuse in Australia. item.description:
Saturday, 12 September 2026

City Hall will be lit Green to support the Eve of National Bilbly Day

National Bilby Day is held each year on the second Sunday in September as a National Day of Awareness and is the only officially gazetted day in Australia dedicated to celebrating one of our iconic native species, the iconic but threatened bilby. The day encourages Australians to ‘Go Green for Bilbies’ by wearing green, hosting events and supporting conservation efforts to help protect the species from extinction. As a flagship species, bilbies help shine a spotlight on biodiversity and the many other threatened species that share their habitat. It is a key opportunity for communities, schools and organisations to learn about the bilby's plight and the work being done to save it, while raising funds and support for on-ground conservation projects.

This Light Up is organised by: Save the Bilby fund Ltd

item.description:
Sunday, 13 September 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Magenta to support World Sepsis Day

World Sepsis Day helps to increase sepsis knowledge and awareness as an important part of combatting sepsis - one of the highest preventable causes of death worldwide. The day is an excellent opportunity to promote knowledge of sepsis and raise awareness, including:
Helping Queenslanders identify the signs and symptoms of sepsis and knowing when to seek help if the condition is not improving or is getting worse.
Providing resources to health professionals to increase the speed at which they can recognise and treat sepsis.
Ensure families and individuals who have been affected by sepsis know that help and support is available.

item.title: National Victims of Crime Day
item.description:
Wednesday, 16 September 2026

Story Bridge will be lit Yellow to support National Victims of Crime Day

Voice for Victims Foundation was founded in 2026 to provide support and guidance to victims of crime - particularly crimes such as violent property invasions, attempted murders and grievous bodily harm. We want all victims to know they can contact us - no matter the crime - and we can either help them ourselves or direct them to the best service for them. As we are new - we want to build awareness for our organisation's services. We also want to continue our advocacy work ensuring victims have voices and aren't invisible. This awareness campaign hopes to not only build awareness for our foundation but also let victims know they are not forgotten.

This Light Up is organised by: Voice for Victims Foundation

item.description:
Thursday, 17 September 2026

Story Bridge will be lit Red to support Blood Cancer and Stem Cell Awareness Month

Every September, we come together for Blood Cancer Awareness Month – a time to shine a light on the thousands of Australians and millions worldwide living with blood cancers and disorders. These conditions can strike anyone, at any age, and for many patients, a stem cell transplant is their only chance of survival. Throughout September, Stem Cell Donors Australia is raising awareness of blood cancers and disorders, culminating in World Marrow Donor Day on Saturday 19 September 2026 – a global event that honours the generosity of volunteer donors and highlights the urgent need for more people to step forward.

item.title: ITP Awareness Week - LightUp4ITP
item.description:
Tuesday, 22 September 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Purple to support ITP Awareness Week - LightUp4ITP

Global ITP Awareness Week (21 to 27 September 2026), is dedicated to raising public awareness of the rare autoimmune blood disorder Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP) and to highlighting the ITP patient experience. ITP is a rare autoimmune disorder in which the body’s immune system attacks healthy platelets and/or suppresses platelet production, resulting in low platelet counts. Platelets help the blood clot, and individuals with ITP typically have a low platelet count. It affects children and adults. There is no cure. For most people, there is no known cause. ITP Australia and New Zealand's mission is to provide up-to-date information, education, support and advocacy for ITP patients and the ITP community. itpaustralia.org.au

item.description:
Sunday, 27 September 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Gold to support Childhood Cancer Awareness Month

September is Childhood Cancer Awareness Month.
The initiative aims to raise awareness of childhood cancer and unite the community in support of children undergoing treatment, survivors, bereaved families and healthcare professionals. Gold is the internationally recognised colour for childhood cancer awareness and symbolises hope, courage and solidarity. This year's request is inspired by the experiences of Queensland families, including those who relocate to Brisbane for treatment, and the illumination of these landmarks will provide a visible show of support, honour children lost to cancer, highlight the importance of continued investment in childhood cancer research and ensure that no child or family facing childhood cancer feels alone.

This Light Up is organised by: Kid's Cancer Project
